text:
incident-bot: Incident created: high GPU queue growth in eu-west-1. Autoscaler failing to provision. Severity: P1. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/1772001123

olivia (SRE on-call): paging on-call, I'm looking. seeing 95% of requests queued for the g4-pool, tail latencies > 8s. errors: 429 throttle.

mike (ML infra): Repro: after yesterday's model rollout (v2.3.1) we see per-request memory for kv-cache up ~30% and seq len distribution shifted right. autoscaler logs show provisioning requests stuck in pending due to quota check timeout.

raj (runtime): dumping autoscaler logs, paste:
```
2026-03-14T09:22:11Z ERROR provisioner: request failed: quota-approval-timeout
2026-03-14T09:22:17Z WARN scale: desired=40 running=28 pending=12
2026-03-14T09:22:20Z INFO router: queue-length=4820 avg-latency=7.9s
```

emily (prod-eng): customer impact: a handful of mid-market customers are seeing elevated 429s and truncation. CS alerted. We need mitigation ASAP.

carlos (support): I've started collecting customer tickets, high priority ones: acct-42, acct-77 reporting failed generation and high cost spikes. Sent temporary notice.

olivia (SRE on-call): immediate actions: 1) enable emergency fallback routing to v2.2.x variant, 2) increase hard reject threshold to avoid unbounded queue, 3) attempt manual scale of dedicated reserved pool if quota allows. Starting step 1 now.

mike (ML infra): can do fallback by toggling model routing flag. Pushing config now. Note: v2.2 uses smaller kv-cache footprint, should reduce per-request GPU memory.

deploy-bot: Rollout request queued by mike at 09:28 UTC: toggle-routing v2.3.1 -> v2.2 for eu-west-1.

raj (runtime): increased reject threshold: requests now rejected after 3000 queue length (was 10k). This reduces head-of-line waiting. Expect 429s to go up but latency to fall.

mike (ML infra): routing toggle done. Traffic for public-prod-eu now split 70/30 favoring v2.2. Monitoring KV mem and queue.

olivia (SRE on-call): monitoring metrics: queue length dropping from 4800 -> 800 in 12min. avg latency down to 1.9s. GPU utilization still high on nodes that remain but no new pending provisions.

emily (prod-eng): can we estimate how much extra GPU capacity the v2.3.1 rollout added? we need to know whether rollout changed context length defaults or altered kv-cache retention.

mike (ML infra): v2.3.1 includes context-length enforcement fix that accidentally disabled prefix truncation for some prompts and bumped default kv_cache_keep=TRUE in the config. That increased per-session KV sizes. We're opening a rollback PR.

carlos (support): CS asked for an ETA to share with affected customers. Any idea of RTO?

olivia (SRE on-call): short-term: fallback routing should restore service within 20-30m; medium-term: revert v2.3.1 or patch kv-cache config and re-roll in controlled canary. I'll hand off to mike/raj for the rollback.

mike (ML infra): starting rollback PR and will coordinate canary -> wholesale if canary looks good. Initial patch will force kv_cache_keep=false and re-enable prefix truncation.

raj (runtime): also found autoscaler bug: when pending provision exceeds 10 nodes and external quota check returns slow, the provisioner enters exponential backoff instead of continuing to try. I'll raise hotfix to cap backoff and add more aggressive retry on quota-check failures.

deploy-bot: Hotfix job submitted by raj at 09:46 UTC: autoscaler-provisioner-backoff-fix. CI pass queued.

olivia (SRE on-call): handoff: I'm pausing active paging - on-call next is mike for infra side and raj for runtime fixes. If queue grows >2000 re-page SRE.

liz (customer-success): I'll send a brief status note to impacted customers: "We've routed traffic to a stable model variant and are working on a rollback/patch; expected restoration within 30 mins, follow-up with postmortem."

emily (prod-eng): followups: 1) schedule postmortem, include rollout checklist addendum about kv-cache defaults; 2) add autoscaler unit test for quota-check slow path; 3) add monitoring alert for sudden avg per-request GPU-memory spike.

mike (ML infra): confirmed routing fallback held; queue stable ~600; starting rollback canary now.

olivia (SRE on-call): closing incident channel for active mitigation; leave thread open for postmortem notes. Marking severity degrade to P2 while rollback in progress.

carlos (support): updating support tickets and marking customers contacted.

mike (ML infra): rollback canary passed in eu-west-1 small subset, no regression on latency or cost. proceeding to full rollout at 10:12 UTC.

raj (runtime): autoscaler backoff hotfix merged and deployed to canary at 10:05 UTC. Observed faster provisioning attempts; pending=0 after scale-up.

olivia (SRE on-call): final check: queue < 200, avg latency 0.9s, 429s back to baseline. Closing active incident at 10:30 UTC. Postmortem owner: emily.

liz (customer-success): follow-up email sent with apology and link to incident page.

emily (prod-eng): creating postmortem doc and action items. I'll include timeline, root cause (kv_cache default change + autoscaler backoff), remediation (revert config, autoscaler fix, rollout checklist), and owners/timelines.

incident-bot: Incident status updated to resolved by olivia at 10:30 UTC. Tags: autoscale, gpu, rollout, kv-cache, mitigation.
